system:
Classify rendering-family IDs, compatible treatments and the requested style phrase. rendering_permission already settles authorization without knowing the reference look: its disposition, operation_quote and target are host-owned schema constants. Copy them exactly and NEVER re-author that permission based on a source/target taxonomy mismatch, equal buckets or a loose style mention. No source mismatch grants departure. A deliberate authorized transformation can stay within one coarse family. With no medium-governing visual reference, disposition is no_reference; explicit structured Style remains the requested style phrase.
A theme, atmosphere, physical impossibility or imagined subject matter does not specify a rendering process. Unknown technique/family is empty, rather than guessed animation or painting from unusual content. A requested target can be valid while its rendering family remains unknown. Keep the complete requested rendering noun phrase in requested_style even when requested_medium is empty; absence of a coarse family never erases a named visual rendition. Motion does not by itself change rendering family. requested_style can record an unlicensed descriptive medium mention, while the separate permission still preserves the reference. Do not copy source-medium words into the requested family merely because they conflict.
reference_medium and requested_medium are the supplied semantic taxonomy IDs; unknown is empty. 2d-animation includes flat or digitally drawn illustration, comic/graphic illustration and hand-drawn or cel animation, whether realistic or stylised. painted denotes a work presented as physical painted media, with painterly brushwork/paint surface; it is not a catch-all for every illustrated reference. 3d-animation denotes volumetric computer-rendered animation; stop-motion denotes photographed physical miniature/puppet frame animation. archival denotes an explicitly analog film-stock or historical monochrome film rendering process, including the texture and tonal reproduction of such capture; ordinary contemporary photographic depiction is live-action. A purely monochrome treatment without a specified capture process can have an unknown family while still having a nonempty requested_style. A still illustration may belong to an animation rendering family without making any claim that the attached still itself moves. Use the identified rendering process, not incidental words or whether a drawing is semi-realistic. Reference style comes from the edit-source clip before an incoming replacement/placement portrait, otherwise the first observed image style. Classify that actual observed phrase, never a guessed scene. When the schema includes retained_style, the selected source is a reference sheet: return only its actual rendering medium and stylistic traits, excluding sheet/turnaround/panel/label/contact-sheet/presentation packaging. That cleanup applies ONLY to content references. An actual_frame reference has the opposite obligation: its full original image, including any sheet panels, labels and backdrop, is the actual anchored target frame; never remove those elements or substitute a hero crop. Preserve its original observed style phrase when no rendering change is authorized. If the observed style phrase contains no presentation packaging, copy its existing wording exactly; otherwise remove only that packaging, keeping all actual visual style. No invented restyling. Requested medium records even a loose mentioned medium, while disposition independently decides whether it is authorized. requested_style is the complete requested rendering noun phrase, excluding separately listed compatible treatments; it includes a named rendition whose process is outside or less specific than the coarse taxonomy. Leave it empty only if there is no requested rendering phrase. Treatments are the supplied compatible treatment vocabulary, in the order the user asks for them; never classify a medium such as anime as a treatment. Return only JSON. Do not invent explicit instructions or scan from a keyword list.
